provenance: real Wisconsin breast-cancer diagnostic measurements (UCI / scikit-learn, CC-BY-4.0)
attribution: Wolberg, Mangasarian, Street & Street, 'Breast Cancer Wisconsin (Diagnostic)', UCI Machine Learning Repository (1993), doi:10.24432/C5DW2B, CC BY 4.0.
modifications: Eight of the 30 columns, standardised with constants fitted on the first 398 rows (scikit-learn order) and rounded to 5 decimals; class recoded to 1 = malignant (the source codes 0 = malignant); split into those 398 rows and the last 171. samples_by_space.raw keeps the eight columns in source units, and heldout.plane mean radius and mean texture, rounded to 4 significant figures.
real_model: logistic regression over the eight shipped WDBC columns, fitted on the 398 rows in `samples`; the 171 rows in `heldout` were not used to fit it or its scaler
fit_note: the regression and its scaler were fitted on rows 0 to 397 of the 569-row cohort, and these are rows 398 to 568.
scaling: StandardScaler fitted on the first 70% of the full 569-row cohort (rows 0 to 397) by qsh.data.loaders.load_breast_cancer, which is where this file's feature definition comes from; those are exactly the rows in `samples`, so no held-out row contributed to the constants.

heldout.note: Rows 398 to 568 of the 569-row cohort in scikit-learn's order, which the regression in `model` was never fitted on and its scaler never saw. 22.8% malignant, against 43.5% in the fitting rows: WDBC's order is not perfectly exchangeable, and the split is the loader's fixed prefix rather than a stratified draw. The browser scores these rows under CKKS.
heldout.split: the last 171 of the 569 rows in scikit-learn's order, 22.8% malignant against 43.5% in the fitting rows (a fixed prefix split, not a stratified draw)

eda.note: Per-column statistics of the rows shipped in this file. `degenerate` names columns that carry effectively no signal and `duplicates` names pairs that are the same column twice; both are kept rather than removed so the feature order stays the one the backend, the registry and the published weights all use.
